name: Dr. Roshan (MCC point of contact — confirm full name)
org: Malabar Cancer Centre (MCC), Thalassery, Kannur, Kerala
pilot_objective: Turn MCC's existing real-time PCR DPYD dataset (~400-500 patients) plus toxicity follow-up into a genotype-to-toxicity map. Identify Grade 3+ fluoropyrimidine-toxicity patients who were negative on the current 7-variant PCR panel (missed-risk cases), assess whether the panel should add South-Asian candidate variants, and scope a joint Indian-cohort publication.
expected_cohort_size: ~400-500 DPYD-tested oncology patients (5-FU / capecitabine; colorectal, head & neck, breast, gastric)
target_timeline: Phase 1 (anonymized PCR + toxicity spreadsheet -> deterministic classification + discordance review): 4-6 weeks from data handoff. Phase 2 (PCR-negative / toxicity-positive discovery subset): contingent on Phase 1. Phase 3 (publication): post-analysis.
notes: Oncology-first wedge: DPYD -> fluoropyrimidine toxicity. MCC tests on real-time PCR (NOT NGS) with a 7-variant panel — Anukriti must accept structured PCR input, VCF not required. Highest-value question: count of Grade 3+ toxicity among all-7-negative patients. Collaboration framing: MCC = lead clinical institution + owns clinical interpretation; Anukriti = analytical engine + reproducible pipeline + audit trail. Honesty boundary: non-core variants (*9A/rs1801265, *4/rs1801158, *5/rs1801159, *6/rs1801160, M166V/rs2297595) labelled 'outcome-correlation needed', not over-claimed.
